cases.description: A Revit rule filter with an inverted AND (System Classification contains 'Supply' and Mark equals 'zz-no-such-mark') reads back as OR of the negated operators
cases.expected: OR of: System Classification does not contain 'Supply', Mark does not equal 'zz-no-such-mark'
manualSteps: In 'Snowdon Towers Sample HVAC.rvt' (do not save) open View > Filters, create a rule-based filter for Ducts with an AND set inverted to NOT: System Classification contains Supply, Mark equals zz-no-such-mark.
In the Model Context panel Filter tab pick that filter in the source list.
The rule editor shows OR with 'does not contain Supply' and 'does not equal zz-no-such-mark'. Undo the filter creation afterwards.

cases.description: The read-back of that inverted filter counts the same ducts as Revit's own filter
manualSteps: With the filter of HF-01, read the panel count.
Apply the filter to a duplicate of view L3 (do not save) and compare: the ducts that stay visible after 'Filter: visible off' are the complement of the panel count.

cases.description: An inverted rule that has no negated operator (Phase Created greater than a phase) reads as one Unsupported rule
manualSteps: In a scratch copy, create a Ducts rule filter inverted to NOT with System Classification contains Supply and Phase Created is greater than a phase.
Pick it in the panel's source list: the editor shows one 'Unsupported rule' line and the filter is read only.

cases.description: An element id comparison rule (Phase Created greater than) is Unsupported
manualSteps: In a scratch copy, create a Ducts rule filter with Phase Created is greater than a phase.
Pick it in the panel's source list: the rule shows as 'Unsupported rule'.

cases.description: A rule-based Revit filter (Ducts, System Classification contains 'Supply') runs natively in its document
cases.expected: panel ids count = Revit ElementFilter count
manualSteps: In a scratch copy, create a Ducts rule filter System Classification contains Supply.
Pick it in the panel's source list and compare the count with a Duct schedule filtered by System Classification contains Supply.

cases.description: A selection filter returns exactly its stored element ids
manualSteps: In a scratch copy select five ducts and click Save (Selection panel) to create a selection filter.
Pick it in the panel's source list: the count is 5 and Select selects the same five ducts.

cases.description: The source list holds both rule-based and selection filters with their kinds
manualSteps: With the filters of HF-05 and HF-06 in a scratch copy, open the panel's source list.
Both appear under Revit filters; the rule-based one opens rules, the selection one shows its stored elements.
